title: Vegetable Guides — expanded photographic concept collection
scope: 24 new numbered concepts in four six-image sheets (7–30), plus a separate revision of former candidate 5's chin/likeness. No final selection or book integration.
decisions_from_john: The previous focused compositions establish a useful visual approach; build a large contact-sheet collection before selecting the very best image.
Subject and composition must each be clear. One dominant subject, natural crops growing in place or candid working activity. No posed harvest or arranged still life.
VARIETY must include crop types and growing settings, not merely variations of courgettes, leeks and runner beans. Apply the established guidelines across different subjects.
The chin in prior image 5 was inaccurate; check the existing likeness notes and actual photographs.
sequence_note: Sheets A and B explore the initial subjects and were generated before the variety clarification. Sheets C and D add twelve further crop types across greenhouse, home beds, net-supported rows and open allotment beds. All are complete exploratory evidence; none is an instruction to resume a parked production task.
candidate_numbering: 7–30 are new identifiers. Separate 05-John-Chin-Revision.png revises original candidate 5 from set 03. Earlier set numbers 1–6 remain distinct historical candidates.

request.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Correct the likeness of John in ONLY the bottom-right photograph numbered 5 of reference image 1. Return this photograph ALONE as one portrait image at 185:240 proportions, without label, border, text or other panels. Preserve this candidate's framing, camera distance, crouched body position, arm/hand action, olive summer clothing, garden bed, slab path, foreground leaves and soft hedge background. It is a local FACE/CHIN correction, not a redesign or a new portrait.

Reference roles:
1 — four-panel concept sheet, EDIT TARGET. Only bottom-right image 5 is the target. Its lowered face/chin is WRONG. Do not preserve that error.
2 — actual photographic downward-profile reference sheet, required for this edit. Use the real camera views at 0:13 and 1:55/2:20, not the illustrated fourth tile.
3 — exact actual camera FACE-DOWN-LEFT at 0:13. This controls the nose/lip/chin relationship when his head points down-left.
4 — actual FACE-DOWN-BARE camera photograph from above, controlling lower-face width, mouth, cheek and beard shape. Real facial features take priority over the generated likeness.
5 — actual John in summer clothes J02 for olive T-shirt, shorts, mature build and bare head/receding grey hair. Do not copy the gesture.

CRITICAL CORRECTION FROM JOHN'S RECORDED LIKENESS NOTES:
When his head is lowered, his LOWER LIP IS VISIBLY AHEAD OF HIS CHIN. The short grey beard follows a SLOPE BACK TOWARDS HIS THROAT. Little underside of the jaw shows above the collar. His chin does not project forwards underneath the lip. The existing generated image has made a strong forward, rounded/square beard/jaw which is not him. Correct the underlying facial contour, not merely the hair length. Use the real photographed profile: a modest tucked-back chin, short tapered beard blending into throat, no jutting bulb of beard, no square ledge under the mouth, no jutting heroic jaw. Maintain a believable natural face with no overcorrection or caricature. Reproduce his actual high forehead, greying hair, nose, eyes and softly closed mouth rather than a generic bearded gardener.

Keep his head tilted toward the courgette plant, looking down-left, candid and unaware of camera. Preserve the relaxed body pose and entire working garden composition. Soft natural summer daylight, photorealistic texture. Do not beautify, make younger, add a hat, add a smile, change clothes, or enlarge him in frame. Output only this corrected full photographic composition.

Use case: photorealistic-natural. ONE six-photo contact sheet of NEW composition candidates for the Vegetable Guides section opener of a British gardening book.
The user endorses the subjects and photographic approach in reference 1 but wants a LARGE choice of strong compositions before selecting one. Make these six genuinely different camera studies, not slight duplicates. NO PEOPLE IN THIS SHEET.

References:
1 — recent reviewed concept sheet: visual standard and subjects (courgettes, leeks, flowering runner beans). Ignore the human panel and printed labels. It is not a template to copy.
2 H31 — actual home garden: true courgette growth, soil and plant texture.
3 A43 — actual allotment leek bed: anatomy, irregular growth and soil.
4 A31 — actual allotment bean row and natural small-plot scale; summer growth may develop, but crop out distant structures.
5 — actual bamboo camera comparison sheet: use the real photographs for slender tapering bamboo, small nodes, irregular shafts, green wire ties and believable support geometry. No diagrams or contact-sheet content inside a photo.

OUTPUT FORMAT: ONE landscape, nearly square sheet approx 1660 wide × 1500 high, 3 columns × 2 rows. Six equal PORTRAIT photos, each approximately 520 wide × 675 high, matching 185:240 proportions. Narrow warm-white gutters and separate little numbering strips under the photos. Label top row 7, 8, 9; bottom row 10, 11, 12. Only these six numerals, outside images. No text overlays or titles.

Shared visual brief: authentic small UK kitchen-garden/allotment crops growing IN PLACE, excellent natural editorial photography, strong single subject, no arranged harvest, no pots/sheds/sky/greenhouses/houses competing in background. Realistic botanical anatomy, fruits attached at correct nodes with correct stems, varied leaves and gaps, mild natural wear. Crops healthy but not pristine uniform specimens. Natural soft daylight with credible optical depth, restrained natural colour, no HDR/CGI/painting, no staged droplets. A quiet darker upper area where natural will help later white titles; do NOT invent a blank black panel. Keep the principal subject away from trim and bottom 12%.

7 — COURGETTE, THE LOW SIDE VIEW. Focus on one normal young dark-green courgette growing diagonally out from its rooted crown, photographed just above soil from the side. A fading blossom on the fruit tip and one fresh yellow flower slightly behind. A broad leaf makes a gentle shaded canopy, other courgette foliage soft behind. Fruit and its natural attachment sharp, no bean leaves, no oversized marrow. This has an intimate low-camera feel and a clear bright fruit/flower against muted foliage.
8 — COURGETTE, LOOKING INTO THE PLANT. A quite different gently overhead portrait looking down through a natural gap in large imperfect leaves to two differently sized attached courgettes and a yellow flower near the lower-middle. The overlapping leaves create an asymmetric frame, some dark earth visible. The fruits must still dominate, not disappear. No perfect radial leaf arrangement or giant unstructured pile. The viewer discovers the crop where it grows.
9 — LEEKS, LOW ROW RHYTHM. A near-ground portrait view with one handsome ordinary leek in the lower-middle foreground, its green-white shaft entering dark soil, its leaves opening irregularly. Unequal plants recede diagonally at different distances, far plants softly focused; all the background is leek leaves, no sky or scenery. Gentle light along leaf edges. Real asymmetry, not identical upright fans.

10 — LEEKS, GRAPHIC DIAGONAL FROM ABOVE. A raised oblique view across several growing leeks, cool blue-green straps diagonally crossing warm brown soil. A visually clear repeated crop theme with a small group of sharp plants and the rest gently receding. Rows and gaps remain imperfect and believable, naturally loose leaf tips, no visible unrelated objects. Distinctly more pattern/soil-driven than 9 while still photographic and readable as leeks.
11 — RUNNER BEANS, FLOWERS FIRST. An intimate portrait of one natural scarlet runner-bean flower raceme and two or three slim developing pods nestled among real trifoliate bean foliage. Small varied blossoms and buds attached on stems, not a bouquet. Weathered narrow bamboo secondary near one side, unobtrusive green tie. In-focus red flowers around middle-height with softly layered green beans behind, no visible shed or sky. Strong colour focus, still natural.
12 — RUNNER BEANS, THROUGH A LEAF WINDOW. A wider oblique close view through two softly out-of-focus leaves in the near foreground to a few hanging runner-bean pods on their vine, with modest scattered scarlet blossoms along the row. Single crop fills frame. Slim canes recede naturally, pods uneven length and slight curl. The gap and hanging pods provide the subject; flowers are accents. Avoid a symmetric arch or tunnel, avoid clutter and visible buildings.

Six different camera positions and compositions, same believable natural photographic family. No humans, no harvested produce, no table arrangements. Make the six portraits feel worth comparing for a full-page photograph.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create ONE NEW sheet of SIX photographic composition candidates for a British gardening book, numbered 13–18. User seeks a large pool of alternatives, natural growing crops or candid John at work, always ONE clear theme. This sheet has three crop views and three human working scenes. Explore DIFFERENT framing and distance, not repeats of earlier images.

References:
1: recent plants-only contact sheet, for natural photographic character, crop anatomy and concept continuity. DO NOT duplicate its panels or numbering.
2 H31: actual home garden camera view. Correct planted bed, slab path alongside greenhouse, low pale wall/hedge, actual leaves and lived-in small garden scale. Use supported bed/path relationship for all John scenes but choose framing that EXCLUDES competing pots, greenhouse, trough and buildings.
3 LOOKDOWN: mandatory real downward-profile photo sheet. Camera panels at 0:13,1:55,2:20 control John's face; ignore illustrated tile, hat and winter clothes.
4 FACE-DOWN-LEFT: actual 0:13 camera crop, definitive downward-left silhouette. This is the identity authority, NOT any generated predecessor.
5 J02: real John, olive T-shirt and olive shorts, mature body, receding greying hair, short grey beard. Same summer clothes and bare head in all three human photos. No microphone, no presentation gesture.

CHIN CORRECTION MUST APPLY TO EVERY HUMAN PHOTO:
John has pointed out our earlier generated chin was wrong. In a lowered head, his lower lip is VISIBLY AHEAD OF THE CHIN, short grey beard slopes BACK TOWARDS THE THROAT, little underside of jaw shows above collar. No square shelf below mouth, no forward rounded tuft, no jutting strong jaw. Follow the photographed silhouette in reference4 and photographic parts of reference3 exactly; natural moderate chin, not exaggerated receding caricature. Head down-left in each human image, so this source angle applies. Accurate real face, not a generic bearded man.

OUTPUT: ONE nearly square LANDSCAPE contact sheet, approx1660 wide ×1500 high; THREE columns × TWO rows. Six equal portrait photographs about520wide×675high, aspect185:240. Narrow off-white margins/gutters. Only numerals 13,14,15 under top row and16,17,18 under bottom row, outside images. No other text.

13 — COURGETTE, A WHOLE PLANT BUT ONE VISUAL CENTRE. Medium-distance portrait from a slightly raised oblique angle. A single growing courgette plant with one visible dark-green fruit and fresh yellow flower near its crown, overlapping broad leaves making a loose diagonal, roots in dark garden soil. More breathing room than a macro, still crops only. Clear dominant fruit/flower, other leaves support it. No bean foliage or other crop types. Include a few mild insect holes and older leaf edges as in ordinary life, no perfect circular symmetry.
14 — LEEKS, LEAF RHYTHM WITH CLOSE DETAIL. A different portrait that emphasises the elegant flat blue-green leek leaves crossing diagonally and turning in light. Show two or three lower shafts rooting in soil in the lower half, with one foreground leaf naturally framing the left side and softer leek rows behind. Strong coherent single crop, no clutter or sky. Individual plants varied, organic garden soil, no repeated fans. Soft bright overcast light brings subtle green tones without gloss.
15 — RUNNER BEANS, FLOWERING ROW FROM A STEP BACK. A medium-close oblique view along living runner beans: several scarlet flower clusters at natural different heights, some pods, overlapping trifoliate leaves on slender bamboo. Framed a little wider than reference1's close-ups but omit ALL buildings, people, sky and unrelated objects. One foreground vine is dominant, rest recedes, enough gaps to feel real. Flower colour draws the eye through the crop, not a uniform floral wallpaper.

16 — JOHN, SMALLER IN THE GARDEN FRAME. Environmental portrait of John crouching on the actual slab path, looking down-left, gently parting one courgette leaf. He occupies about45–50% of photo height, positioned in the middle/right, with foreground courgette leaves guiding to his hands and face. Garden plants subordinate to the clear human activity. Soft quiet hedge behind, no pots, shed, trough, greenhouse or structures. No eye contact or camera smile. Moderate optical depth; whole action readable. Keep head, hands and feet safely inside the portrait.
17 — JOHN, STANDING AND LEANING INTO THE JOB. Fresh candid composition, same real home bed/path relationship. John stands on the path and bends naturally forward a little at hips to check a courgette leaf with one hand, other hand resting on his thigh for balance; body weight and joints credible. Frame from shoes upward with enough room above; he is not looming close. Left-facing lowered three-quarter profile matching actual face refs. Medium-distance, low foreground foliage and plain soft hedge background. All attention on the plant, no display/presentation gesture. Maintain a single human subject theme.
18 — JOHN, A QUIET KNEELING MOMENT. A different slightly lower camera view at bed height: John kneeling on one knee on the slab path, side-on facing left with head down, removing a small unwanted seedling by hand from beside a growing leafy crop. Modest action, ordinary scale, one working hand near soil and other resting on bent knee, nothing staged. Frame wider than a portrait to include the approach of the bed edge and a few leaves in near foreground; John still unmistakably the focus, about55% of frame height. Background soft and free of competing structures. No tools, buckets or arranged produce.

For all: high-quality convincing natural camera photography in ordinary soft summer daylight, no HDR/cinematic effects, no fantasy garden perfection. Growing crops still attached correctly, varied realistic plants and soil gaps, no harvested arrangements. Gentle meaningful optical focus, not smeared cutout blur. Photos13–15 have no people. 16–18 each show ONLY John, true likeness with corrected chin. Retain quiet areas for future white titles where naturally possible but no title now; don't create artificial black voids. Keep bottom12% expendable. Distinct compositions with a coherent book-photography character.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
ONE contact sheet of SIX DISTINCT full-page gardening photograph concepts, numbered 19–24. The user's central request is VARIETY OF CROP TYPES AND GROWING SETTINGS. The successful earlier work established compositional principles; it must NOT restrict us to courgettes, leeks and runner beans. This sheet contains six completely different new crops. Each photograph has ONE instantly clear crop subject and a natural real-growing setting. No people.

Reference roles:
1 is the earlier four-panel sheet for quality, naturalness, strong single-subject compositions and uncluttered photographic backgrounds ONLY. Do not repeat its crops, human, compositions or numbering.
2 H35 actual greenhouse interior: real aluminium glazing, brick/low block growing beds, central paving, pot/bed texture, tomato vines and seasonal plants. Use this authentic ordinary small greenhouse setting in 19, tightly reframed to the crop.
3 H36 actual second summer greenhouse angle, plant scale and soft screening. Real materials, not a luxury glass conservatory.
4 H44 actual home lettuce bed: true green/burgundy lettuce variation, soil spacing, modest productive garden, ordinary path/bed edge.
5 A44 actual summer allotment: planted soil strips, fine crop netting, modest narrow grass/brick access paths and working-plot scale. Use texture/setting for outdoor cropped views without architecture.

FORMAT: ONE nearly-square LANDSCAPE contact sheet approx1660wide×1500high, 3columns×2rows. Each photo portrait185:240 proportions (~520wide×675high), equal size, narrow warm-white gutters. Top row numbers19,20,21; bottom row22,23,24. Numbers outside and below photos. No other text.

ONE SUBJECT PER PHOTO. Visually interesting setting changes, while background landmarks stay subordinate. Real soft daylight, credible optical focus, naturally unequal healthy plants with only mild wear and occasional small nibbles. No masses of holes or diseased leaves. No staged produce, tables, harvest baskets or flower arrangements. Anatomically credible crops rooted/growing where appropriate. No giant vegetables, artificial identical leaves, heavy HDR, cinematic grading or excessive fake blur. Natural rich colours, inviting but ordinary.

19 — TOMATOES IN THE GREENHOUSE. Portrait at truss height in the actual small greenhouse setting. A single ordinary tomato truss with 4–6 unequal fruits at green/orange/red ripening stages is the focus, connected correctly by calyces and stems to a living vine. Some serrated tomato foliage and restrained cane/string support, all real plant architecture. Soft silver-grey glasshouse lines far behind give a new setting, but no broad architecture or pots competing. Warm transmitted daylight on fruit, gentle green shadows, natural skins not waxed perfect spheres. Room around the truss, no endless abundance.
20 — COLOURFUL CHARD IN A HOME BED. Low oblique view INTO a living chard clump, with a few red, yellow and pale stems rising from distinct rooted crowns and rippled rich green leaves. A bright red stem and its leaf form the centre, other stems support the composition. Dark cultivated soil visible at base, a modest bed-edge hint soft at one side. Naturally unequal leaves, attractive veining and slight curl; not rainbow candy colours, not laid-out harvested stalks. Different texture and mood from tomatoes, diffused outdoor daylight.
21 — RED CABBAGE AT THE ALLOTMENT. Close three-quarter slightly raised view of one compact purple-red cabbage head still growing, nested in its broad matte glaucous outer leaves. Pale veins and deep purple centre form an elegant focal pattern. A second cabbage recedes softly, a very quiet hint of protective mesh in the distance conveys allotment without obstructing the main plant. Earth beneath, no sky, shed or trees. A few honest outer-leaf nibbles only. Natural tightly wrapped central head, not a giant flower or perfectly radial rosette.

22 — BEETROOT AT SOIL LEVEL. Intimate near-ground portrait of two or three differently sized beetroot shoulders naturally swelling partly above the soil, roots still underground, burgundy stems and green/red-veined leaves rising from correct crowns. One larger root low-centre with smaller neighbours receding, no dug-up roots or exposed taproots. Rich earthy textures, only light natural soil at contact, leaves form a gentle background. Not uniformly spherical marbles, no row arranged for display. Overcast garden light and a quieter darker upper leaf area.
23 — A LIVING LETTUCE BED. A softly elevated diagonal view along a natural grouping of green and burgundy loose-leaf lettuces, based on real H44 planting character. A green lettuce with ruffled centre anchors the lower-middle; a few unequal red lettuces behind add colour and rhythm. Plants have separate rooted crowns, different size/opening and visible soil gaps. Crop close enough to omit hoops, greenhouse and other crops; all one coherent salad-leaf theme. Natural lushness, not a formal ornamental bedding pattern or a perfect alternating grid.
24 — PEAS ON THEIR NET. At the edge of a modest allotment pea row, several fine curling tendrils hold an open square garden net; one clear cluster of fresh green pea pods and a few small white pea flowers is the subject. Pods are rounded and light compared with runner beans, correctly attached at nodes; delicate paired pea leaves and stipules, NOT giant bean leaves. Net is thin and unobtrusive, background pea foliage softly layered, a little distant earthy warmth. Gentle light across a pod seam. No bamboo arches or buildings.

Portraits intended eventually for a large white section title; keep a natural quiet patch where feasible and important detail clear of trim/bottom12%, but this is subject/composition exploration and no titles should be generated. SIX DIFFERENT CROP TYPES, different camera heights and settings, all one consistent high-quality photographic family. Plants growing naturally, never a harvested still life.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Create ONE contact sheet of SIX DISTINCT photographic candidates for a British gardening book section opener, numbered25–30. This sheet broadens CROP TYPES AND GROWING SETTINGS, not merely camera variations of the same vegetables. Four plant-only photographs and two candid scenes of the actual gardener John. Each has ONE strong subject and a clear photographic composition.

ACTUAL REFERENCES:
1 H36: John's real small greenhouse in summer, aluminium glazing, shading, pots, low masonry beds and narrow central paved aisle. Use this ordinary working greenhouse character for25 and29. It is supporting setting, not the main theme. Crop/blur clutter and irrelevant architecture.
2 A31: actual Cornish allotment, cultivated strips, narrow access paths, modest planting density. Source for outdoor soil/materials/scale, NOT an instruction to repeat bean crops or show sheds.
3 LOOKDOWN: mandatory downward-profile reference sheet. Its actual camera stills at0:13,1:55,2:20 control John's face; ignore illustrated tile, hat and winter clothes.
4 FACE-DOWN-LEFT: original close camera crop facing down-left. This silhouette is definitive for lower lip, chin and beard in29 and30.
5 J02: actual John for identity/body/receding grey hair and olive summer T-shirt and shorts. Bareheaded, omit microphone. Do NOT copy the gesture toward camera.

CRITICAL LIKENESS: earlier generated chin was wrong. With head lowered, LOWER LIP VISIBLY AHEAD OF CHIN; short grey beard slopes back towards throat, little underside of jaw above collar. No forward square shelf, no protruding rounded beard/tuft or strong jutting jaw. Match actual reference4 rather than any generated gardener. Preserve natural face, not an exaggerated receding chin. Both human pictures show left-facing lowered head so real reference applies. No looking at camera.

FORMAT: one almost-square LANDSCAPE contact sheet approximately1660wide×1500high, THREE columns×TWO rows. Equal portrait photos at185:240 ratio (~520wide×675high). Narrow off-white borders/gutters and separate number strips under panels. Top row25,26,27; bottom row28,29,30. These numbers are the only text; no overlays.

25 — AUBERGINE IN A SMALL GREENHOUSE. No person. One beautiful ordinary deep-purple aubergine fruit hangs naturally from a sturdy living potted plant, fuzzy pale-green calyx and thick correct pedicel. A smaller fruit and a modest violet star-shaped flower subtly behind; broad slightly fuzzy leaves frame it. One dominant fruit, not a huge market display. Soft diffused greenhouse daylight, realistic skin reflection not mirror polish. Background grey-green glazing lines and foliage softly recede; pot edge only a subdued grounding hint. An intimate distinctive purple/green photograph.
26 — SWEETCORN IN AN OPEN SUMMER BED. No person. At cob height among growing sweetcorn, focus on one naturally husked green ear with brown-gold silks attached at a stalk node, with long maize leaves arching at unequal angles. A second plant and tassels recede softly into greenery; no sky or distant buildings. Do NOT peel husks to display kernels; this is the living crop. Real scale, leaves neither perfect ribbons nor cloned repeats. Gentle warm daylight crossing the silks gives a clear focal point, the setting feels tall and airy.
27 — ONIONS RIPENING IN ALLOTMENT SOIL. No person. Low three-quarter portrait of three unequal golden-brown onion bulbs swelling partly above dry cultivated soil, still rooted, papery outer skins with natural fine wrinkles, attached tubular leaves softening and bending as the crop matures. One larger bulb forward, smaller neighbours at different depths. No lifted harvest, no tied bunches, no loose onions placed for a still life, no fully exposed roots. Warm muted earth and gold colour, quieter folded leaves in upper background. Authentic organic growing bed with small gaps.
28 — POTATOES IN FLOWER. No person. Crop-height portrait among a healthy growing potato patch, one small cluster of pale lilac/white five-point flowers with yellow anther centres above distinctive compound potato leaves. A few different-height flowering stems recede softly, enough foliage/earth context to read as a food crop, not a bouquet. No exposed tubers, no decorative pots or other flowers. Fresh natural green, diffused cloudy-day light and gentle depth. Vary foliage honestly, no wallpaper repetition.
29 — JOHN TENDING CUCUMBERS INSIDE HIS GREENHOUSE. Candid environmental portrait, human activity is the SINGLE dominant theme. John stands on the real central paved aisle, body about55–60% photo height, looking down-left as he gently guides a living cucumber vine onto its support string. One modest cucumber hangs nearby as clear gardening context, not a competing display. Medium-distance three-quarter angle, olive summer T-shirt/shorts, mature real body and corrected actual chin from references3/4. Soft green foliage frames him; glazing is a faint out-of-focus cue, not a second architectural subject. Keep whole head/hands inside frame. Natural balanced stance and believable hands, no camera eye contact, no smile/presentation, no tools or harvest props.
30 — JOHN WITH A SPINACH BED AT THE ALLOTMENT. A quiet candid outdoor moment, different setting/height from29. John kneels on one knee at the grassy/paved edge of an open leafy spinach bed, looking down-left, separating an outer leaf with one hand to see new growth while other hand rests on his bent knee. Medium-distance view: human abouthalf photo height, foreground soft spinach leaves lead towards hands and face. Correct ordinary spinach oval-to-arrow-shaped leaves, not giant chard/kale/courgette leaves. Soil and a narrow access edge locate the scene; crop out sheds, houses and unrelated crops so John remains the focus. Same olive summer clothes, accurate chin, bareheaded. No posing or looking at camera.

ALL SIX: photo-quality realistic UK growing conditions, varied SUBJECTS and SETTINGS, strong visual centre, no artificial perfection. Healthy ordinary plants with only occasional tiny imperfections; no shredded leaves or excessive holes. Real attachments, correct plant anatomy, natural spacing, mild soil where appropriate. No HDR, cinematic effects, painted/CGI finish, excessive glossy skins or smeared blur. Realistic soft photographic depth, inviting restrained natural colours. Future large WHITE titles are separate: no titles now, quiet upper area where natural, keep main subjects away from edges and bottom12%. These are six composition candidates, not a designed book page.

source_authority.likeness: Original FACE-DOWN-LEFT at A11 raw camera 0:13, required LOOKDOWN photo sheet, FACE-DOWN-BARE for standalone correction, J02 for summer clothes/body. Camera sources outrank generated predecessors.
source_authority.chin_rule: Lower lip visibly ahead of chin when looking down; short beard slopes back towards throat; little jaw underside visible above collar. Avoid projected rounded or square beard and jutting chin.
source_authority.sites: Actual H31, H35, H36, H44, A31, A43 and A44 views, plus actual cane construction comparison. See exact inputs per generation.
source_authority.planting_assumptions: New crops, growth stages and actions are proposed seasonal scenes using genuine site materials and character. They are not documentary evidence that each crop was photographed in each bed, or at one date.
source_authority.wardrobe: J02 olive T-shirt and shorts, bareheaded; no microphone.
